E1.evidence: The reporter names branch and commit ("branch: ros2", "commit: c052be03fe0bc067fdf0941394a62dcc81925ae8") and shows a screenshot of the launch output containing "Device specified is not available or is not a vaild V4L2 device: `/dev/camera/top_6mm`" followed by the list of available /dev/video0../dev/video5 devices, and `ll /dev/camera/top_6mm` showing it links to ../video0 (https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/issues/298, image https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/assets/46778435/167112d3-3f2f-43c9-9688-4482c214d19f). A downstream maintainer attributes it to a usb_cam change: "usb_camパッケージの変更により`/dev/video*/`以外のデバイス名を認識できなくなりました。" (https://github.com/rt-net/sciurus17_ros/pull/153).

E2.evidence: The reporter's launch package passes a udev-symlink device path through usb_cam's video_device parameter; usb_cam, since PR 286 (commit af45135d, "Check if given v4l2 device exists before opening it"), accepts only names found by enumerating "/dev/video" + std::to_string(i) and otherwise calls rclcpp::shutdown(). The rejected value crosses the parameter boundary, so the failure is not internal. The minimal consumer-side fix is a device-path binding in the launch file (os.path.realpath), but the breakage comes from a provider change to what usb_cam accepts for video_device, which the consumer must follow; the provider later also changed (PR 311 "Resolve Symlinks"), so this is not deployment_wiring.

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: the consumer's symlinked device paths were accepted by usb_cam up to release 0.7.0, which has no availability check; the reported provider revision c052be03 contains the check added by PR 286 (merged 2023-10-28). Issue 310 describes the same effect as a regression: "This worked fine until recently (unfortunately I am not sure which update broke that)." (https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/issues/310).

E4.evidence: Observed startup refusal in the reporter's screenshot: "Device specified is not available or is not a vaild V4L2 device: `/dev/camera/top_6mm`" followed by "Shutting down" (https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/assets/46778435/167112d3-3f2f-43c9-9688-4482c214d19f).

units.name: usb_cam
units.revision_basis: The reporter states "branch: ros2" and "commit: c052be03fe0bc067fdf0941394a62dcc81925ae8" (2023-11-13 merge of PR 292). The reporter's resolution changes only their launch file, so the provider keeps its broken revision.

units.name: robobus_sensor_kit_launch (reporter's camera_top_6mm launch)
units.revision_basis: The reporter runs `ros2 launch robobus_sensor_kit_launch camera_top_6mm.launch.py` (screenshot, log dated 2023-11-16). The public repository https://github.com/pixmoving-moveit/robobus_sensor_kit_launch (last push 2023-09-06) has no camera_top_6mm launch file, so the consumer is described from the issue text: the broken state from the issue body (2023-11-16), the resolved state from the launch file the reporter posted on 2023-11-29 with the added realpath line.

loudness_evidence: The provider refuses the device at activation with its own error and shuts down: "Device specified is not available or is not a vaild V4L2 device: `/dev/camera/top_6mm`" then "Available V4L2 devices are:" and "Shutting down" (reporter's screenshot https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/assets/46778435/167112d3-3f2f-43c9-9688-4482c214d19f; the message text is the RCLCPP_ERROR_STREAM added in af45135d).

resolution.summary: The consumer resolves the udev symlink before passing it to usb_cam: `parameters["video_device"] = os.path.realpath(parameters["video_device"])` in its launch file, so video_device is the canonical /dev/videoN path that usb_cam's enumeration accepts.
resolution.evidence: The reporter, whose setup is identified as usb_cam ros2 commit c052be03, posts the modified launch file saying "In the startup file, add a command to solve this problem" and closes the issue (https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/issues/298#issuecomment-1831120952). The same fix applied to a different consumer, rt-net/sciurus17_ros PR 153 (`{'video_device': os.path.realpath('/dev/chestcamera')}` in sciurus17_vision/launch/chest_camera.launch.py, merged 2024-02-21 as 22ba7f8113d217e43853ca0a79ef5599b8d9877d), was tested by launching on hardware, with no usb_cam revision stated.

notes: Class choice: the same device is named by a udev symlink path on the consumer side and by its canonical /dev/videoN path in usb_cam's enumeration (utils::available_devices builds `"/dev/video" + std::to_string(i)`), so I used representation_convention for the path form of the video_device value; no other class fits (the parameter's declaration `this->declare_parameter("video_device", "/dev/video0");` is unchanged, so not element_retyped). consumer_built_against is inferred: the source gives no earlier usb_cam version for the consumer; I used release tag 0.7.0 (eadb3265e23597b47fcbdc9c6a4b879b102d30f7, 2023-08-31), the last release before PR 286 (merged into ros2 as 64c417fad48fcbb26863328cf6c05f8ff581fd9a on 2023-10-28, first parent a6dfa06f, one commit after 0.7.0), because the consumer's reliance on symlinked device paths matches the behaviour before that check; 0.7.0 already declares all the parameters the consumer sets, including pixel format "uyvy2rgb". Provider-side resolution for the same defect: usb_cam PR 311 "Resolve Symlinks" (merged 2024-01-20 as e2b11abfd5b337311fa6c5fc79ed6f6768b78649, for issue 310), later extended by PR 358 "Correctly resolve symlinks to device paths" (merged 2025-02-08); the PR 311 author notes it "solves only half of the problem" for containers where only the symlink is mounted. Other compositions: rt-net/sciurus17_ros (chest camera launch using /dev/chestcamera) and issue 310's four-camera setup (/dev/camera00) hit the same refusal. The reporter's device path appears only in the title and a screenshot log; the public robobus_sensor_kit_launch repository uses "/dev/video0" in config/camera_top.yaml and has no camera_top_6mm launch. The reporter's posted resolved launch file sets "video_device": "/dev/video0" (a demo value) before applying realpath.
